brewing.notes: A safe starting point for dark tea: rinse once, boiling water, or simmer it the traditional way.

description:
A dark tea from Ehime Prefecture, developed from the local Ishizuchi kurocha tradition.

Treat it as you would any dark tea: rinse it, use boiling water, and buy from someone who can say who pressed it and when.
history: When Ishizuchi kurocha was down to a single producer, a local livelihood-study group took up the technique and turned it into a product under the name Tengu kurocha. Little more is documented about it.
processing: Typical of dark tea: green leaf is piled so that microbes ferment it, then dried and often pressed.
harvest_season: Often made from coarser, later leaf, as with most dark teas.
appearance_dry: Usually dark leaf, loose or pressed into bricks or baskets.
appearance_wet: Usually coarse dark leaf with some stem.
taste_profile: Expect what dark teas usually give: smooth, woody and earthy.
vintage_note: Dark teas are sold by production year and many improve with several years of dry storage.
